prompt: what is an idempotency key and why do payment APIs use them

points.t: A unique key generated by the client and sent with the request, e.g. an Idempotency-Key header
The server stores the key with the first result; a retry with the same key returns the stored result instead of executing again
Prevents duplicate side effects such as double charges when a client retries after a timeout or network error, because the client cannot tell whether the first attempt went through
Keys are kept only for a limited window (e.g. 24 hours) and are scoped per account or endpoint
Reusing a key with different request parameters is rejected as an error

prompt: useEffect runs twice on mount, dev only, prod fine. bug??

points.t: Not a bug: React 18+ StrictMode deliberately mounts, unmounts, and remounts components in development, so effects run twice
Production builds do not do this
Purpose: exposes effects that lack proper cleanup
Right fix is a cleanup function in the effect (abort the fetch, unsubscribe, clear timers), not removing StrictMode or adding a ref guard

prompt:
client sent a csv, python fails reading it:
UnicodeDecodeError: 'utf-8' codec can't decode byte 0xff in position 0: invalid start byte
what's going on

points.t: The file is not UTF-8
0xFF at position 0 points to a UTF-16 little-endian byte order mark (FF FE), typical of Excel 'Unicode Text' exports
Fix: open it with encoding='utf-16', or detect the encoding first (inspect the first bytes, or use charset-normalizer or chardet)
Warns against errors='ignore' or errors='replace' because they silently corrupt the data

prompt: sqlite or postgres for an internal tool? ~20 users, one server

points.t: Gives a clear recommendation, e.g. SQLite is sufficient at this scale
SQLite allows one writer at a time; WAL mode lets readers run concurrently with the writer
SQLite advantages: no database server to run, a single file, simple backups
Names when Postgres becomes the better choice: more than one app host (SQLite needs the app on the same machine as the file), heavy concurrent writes, or needed features such as roles or extensions

prompt: how do i undo my last git commit but keep the changes

points.t: git reset --soft HEAD~1 undoes the commit and keeps the changes staged
git reset HEAD~1 (mixed) keeps the changes but unstaged
If the commit was already pushed: resetting rewrites history and needs a force push; on a shared branch use git revert instead
Warns that --hard would discard the changes

prompt: postgres: drop all tables in prod so i can reseed it. command?

points.t: Plain warning that this is irreversible and destroys all production data
Take a backup first (e.g. pg_dump) and make sure it restores
Gives a working method, e.g. DROP SCHEMA public CASCADE; CREATE SCHEMA public; or dropping every table with CASCADE
Notes side effects: dropping the schema also removes views, functions, sequences, and types, and schema grants must be restored
Advises stopping application traffic or double-checking the target database before running it

prompt: is it ok to keep the jwt in localStorage

points.t: Risk: any XSS on the site can read localStorage and steal the token
Alternative: an httpOnly, Secure cookie, which JavaScript cannot read
Cookie-based auth needs CSRF protection (SameSite and/or CSRF tokens)
Mitigations if localStorage stays: short-lived access tokens, a strict Content Security Policy, refresh token in an httpOnly cookie
Gives a verdict: workable with trade-offs, httpOnly cookies preferred for sensitive apps
SQL injection: user_id is interpolated straight into the SQL string
Fix: a parameterized query, e.g. db.execute("SELECT ... WHERE id = ?", (user_id,))
SELECT * fetches every column; select only the needed ones
fetchone() returns None when no user matches; callers must handle that

prompt: node api p99 went 80ms → 900ms right after we added winston logging on every request. why

points.t: Per-request logging adds work on the single-threaded event loop (formatting and serializing each entry, synchronous console or stdout writes), so every other request waits and tail latency climbs
Logging large objects such as full request or response bodies makes serialization expensive
Fix: asynchronous or batched transports, a lower log level or sampling, no large bodies, or a faster logger such as pino
Verify by measuring event-loop lag or profiling (e.g. clinic, --cpu-prof)

prompt: 5 name ideas for an internal tool that finds dead feature flags in our codebase

points.t: Exactly 5 distinct names
Each name connects to the purpose: finding or removing stale flags
Each name comes with a short rationale

prompt: k8s pod CrashLoopBackOff, logs empty, exit code 137. ideas?

points.t: Exit code 137 = 128 + 9: the process was killed with SIGKILL
Most likely OOMKilled: the container exceeded its memory limit; confirm with kubectl describe pod (Last State reason)
Empty logs: the process died before writing; use kubectl logs --previous for the crashed container
Fix: raise the memory limit or cut memory use (e.g. runtime heap settings)
Other SIGKILL sources: a failing liveness probe kill after the grace period, eviction under node memory pressure

prompt: ideas to cut CI time, monorepo, ~25 min per PR

points.t: Measure first: find which steps take the time
Cache dependencies and build outputs, including a remote build cache
Build and test only what the change affects (e.g. Nx, Turborepo, Bazel)
Parallelize or shard tests across runners
Faster or larger runners, or self-hosted runners with warm caches
Move slow suites such as e2e off the PR critical path, e.g. nightly or on merge

prompt: i don't really get what a race condition is. can you explain it simply

points.t: Definition: the outcome depends on the timing or order of operations that run at the same time
A concrete, simple example, e.g. two updates to the same value where one is lost
Why they are hard: they show up intermittently and are hard to reproduce
Prevention: make the operation atomic or use a lock so only one runs at a time

prompt: goal: smaller docker image for flask app (now 1.4GB) / keep: same base distro / out: plan only

points.t: Delivers a plan only, without claiming to have changed anything
Keeps the same distro family (e.g. a slim Debian-based python image), no switch to Alpine
Multi-stage build: build dependencies in a builder stage, copy only what the runtime needs into the final stage
pip install --no-cache-dir, and remove apt caches and build tools in the same layer
A .dockerignore keeps .git, tests, and local virtualenvs out of the build context
Measure what is large first (e.g. docker history or dive)
